prompt.context: We have a private equity client that is considering purchasing a small company that makes paintball guns called Splat. Sales last year were $50M, net profit was $20M, and they have been growing at 50% per year. The client has asked us for help in evaluating this investment. You and I are the team members who will do the bulk of the thinking and analysis.
prompt.question: How would you evaluate whether or not this paintball gun company (Splat) is a good investment?

clarifying_info.q: What is the size of the paintball gun market?
clarifying_info.a: There are no secondary research reports on the paintball gun market — we will need to estimate it ourselves. Assumptions to use: US population = 300M (US only); 10% of population plays paintball in a given year; 10% of players actually purchase (rather than rent) a gun; average purchaser buys 1 gun per year; average price of a gun = $100.

clarifying_info.q: How fast is the paintball market growing?
clarifying_info.a: The market is growing approximately 20% per year and will continue to do so for the next several years.

clarifying_info.q: How do end customers view Splat relative to competitors?
clarifying_info.a: When surveyed, customers indicated they buy based on reputation for quality. Splat is known as having the best paintball guns on the market. Two other players are viewed quite favorably, but not as highly ranked as Splat.

clarifying_info.q: What retail channels does Splat sell through?
clarifying_info.a: Splat sells through paintball specialty stores and large chains of sports stores such as Galyans, Sports Authority, and Wal-Mart. Sales have been steady through specialty channels but growing approximately 60% per year in large chains.

clarifying_info.q: Why are large-chain sales growing so much faster than the overall market?
clarifying_info.a: Store managers surveyed in large chains report that their overall paintball gun sales are growing at 20%, and Splat is doing slightly better than other brands at about 25% growth. However, over the last few years the chains have been adding Splat to a few stores per year — Splat is now in almost all of those stores, which is the primary driver of the extraordinary growth.

framework: Assess market attractiveness: size the market, understand growth rate and drivers
Assess Splat's competitive position: product quality vs. competitors, customer perception, brand strength
Understand the sources of Splat's 50% growth vs. 20% market growth — decompose by channel and distribution
Evaluate valuation / price paid relative to expected future growth
Identify key risks to the investment thesis

questions.prompt: Estimate the size of the US paintball gun market.
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a bottoms-up market size: US population × participation rate × purchase rate × guns per purchaser × price. Should arrive at $300M and note Splat's implied 20% market share ($50M / $300M).

math.setup: Market size = US population × % who play paintball × % who buy (vs rent) × guns purchased per year × average price
math.answer: Annual US paintball gun market ≈ $300M; Splat has approximately 17–20% market share

questions.prompt: How would you assess Splat's competitive position and explain why its growth (50%) far exceeds market growth (20%)?
questions.guidance: Strong answer decomposes the growth discrepancy into drivers: (1) slight market share gain from brand/quality advantage (~25% organic growth), (2) rapid channel expansion into large retail chains (adding stores, not just same-store growth). Candidate should identify that the store roll-out is largely complete — Splat is now in almost all chain stores — so this tailwind will largely disappear going forward. Future growth should normalise closer to 25% (market growth + modest share gain).

questions.prompt: Given your analysis, what is your overall recommendation on the investment?
questions.guidance: Candidate should synthesise: market is attractive (growing 20%+), Splat has a quality/brand advantage, but the extraordinary 50% growth was partly driven by one-time retail channel expansion now nearly complete. Future growth should be modelled at 20–25%. Investment attractiveness depends on the price paid — client should proceed if returns at 20–25% growth meet their hurdle rate. Should flag key risks.

brainstorming.prompt: What risks would you highlight for this investment?

categories.name: Market / demand risks
ideas: Paintball may be a fad — participation could plateau or decline
Seasonal or demographic shifts reduce player base

categories.name: Competitive / brand risks
ideas: Brand perceptions can shift quickly, eroding Splat's quality premium
New entrants with lower-cost or higher-tech guns could undercut Splat
Larger incumbents could respond aggressively on price or distribution

categories.name: Safety / legal risks
ideas: Injury or death caused by a Splat gun creates product liability exposure
Injury from any brand could trigger regulatory action or reduce overall participation
Negative media coverage of paintball safety could suppress demand

categories.name: Channel / distribution risks
ideas: Channel expansion tailwind is exhausted — large chains already carry Splat in almost all stores
Retailer de-listing or shelf-space reduction would hurt growth disproportionately

categories.name: Financial / deal risks
ideas: Valuation may be inflated due to transient 50% growth rate
High profit margin (40%) may be unsustainable if competition intensifies
Private equity hold period may not align with market maturation timeline

recommendation: Splat is an attractive investment IF acquired at a price that reflects normalised growth of 20–25% per year, not the recent 50% growth rate
The business has genuine strengths: strong brand, best-in-class product perception, and a growing addressable market
However, a significant portion of recent growth came from one-time retail channel expansion that is now largely complete — future growth will be more modest
risks: Paintball participation is fad-sensitive; a decline in popularity would compress both market size and Splat's revenues
Safety incidents (with any brand) could damage the category and create legal liability for Splat
Brand leadership can erode quickly if competitors invest in product quality or marketing
next_steps: Negotiate a valuation that uses 20–25% forward growth assumptions, not trailing 50%
Conduct customer and retailer survey to validate brand health and confirm distribution is fully saturated
Assess regulatory and product liability environment; review insurance coverage
Model downside scenarios assuming market growth reverts to 10% or participation flatlines
